findings.excerpt: Construction tells you how the towel is made, while weave describes the way its fibres are arranged. Microfibre is a prominent car-drying option, and waffle weave is another format people search for, but the name alone does not establish which will perform better. Check the actual product description rather than assuming every towel with the same broad label is identical.
findings.reason: Proof-oriented wording is useful internally but sounds rigid in customer-facing advice.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the delivery only; do not add, remove or strengthen the claim.

I would look at GSM alongside the rest of the specification rather than using it to declare one towel better, safer or faster.

findings.excerpt: Look at the edge finish as well as the main fabric. Edging is a separate part of the towel’s construction, so it deserves its own check when you compare product descriptions. Do not assume the centre fabric tells you how the whole towel is finished.
findings.reason: Clinical definition-plus-instruction phrasing is accurate but more formal than the direct, practical target voice.

findings.excerpt: My view is that it makes the most sense for someone who actively wants a large, dense towel and is comfortable handling the extra weight once it is saturated.
